articles.title: Make it pop: contrast of colour AND shine
articles.summary: Pop comes from neighbours that differ: a complementary colour pair, plus a shine difference such as candy or metal beside matte, with one loud hero panel. Saturation alone does not do it.
articles.what: When a buyer says "make it pop", "pop more" or "it looks flat", the cure is contrast between neighbours, not more colour. Put a deep glossy candy or metal next to a flat matte of the opposite colour, keep one hero area loud (hood, roof or the big side) and let everything else stay calm so the eye has somewhere to land.
when: The car looks flat or boring in the preview.
A buyer asks for more punch without changing the colours.
how: Pick the hero area (the hood, roof or the biggest side panel) and the two colours that sit opposite each other: blue and orange, black and hot pink, white and red.

Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.

Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Candy (metal 200, roughness 15, coat 16). Set BASE COLOR to Use solid color and choose a deep colour for the hero. Candy is the glossy one.

Add a second zone for the neighbouring area. Choose Matte from the same shelf (metal 0, roughness 200, coat 160) with the opposite colour. Drag the hero zone above the matte zone in the left column so it wins where they meet. A new zone is added at the BOTTOM of the list and the higher zone wins, so the hero zone has to be dragged up.
Add trim as a third zone: PICK COLOR FROM CAR on the stripe or accent colour, choose Satin Chrome (metal 250, roughness 45, coat 40) and set BASE COLOR to Use source paint (spec only).
Open the preview strip: R METAL is the metal, G ROUGH the roughness (dark is mirror), B COAT the clearcoat (16 is the glossiest). Check them against the numbers above.
Judge it small. If the car reads as a clear two-value picture at arm's length, stop. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing, and judge it in the sim at an angle to the sun.

deep.heading: Why saturation alone fails
deep.body: The owner's favourite finish out of 50 measured shelf entries did not win on saturation, which was only mid-pack. It won because neighbouring bands were a true colour opposite and the shine layer was the colour-opposite of the paint. Plain saturation just makes a louder blob.

deep.heading: Shine contrast is half of pop
deep.body: Candy is metal 200, roughness 15, coat 16; Matte is metal 0, roughness 200, coat 160. In the sim the candy mirrors the sky while the matte soaks it up, so the pair separates even if the two colours were close. A zone with one shine everywhere reads as one flat blob however bright.

deep.heading: Pop must survive distance
deep.body: Many mid-tones (browns, dull teals, greys) turn to mud when the car is small. Two or three clear values with one accent hold up from far away; five colours look cheap.

faq.q: How do I make my livery pop?
faq.a: Put one deep glossy candy or metal area next to a matte area of the opposite colour, and keep the rest calm. Add chrome only as trim.

faq.q: It looks flat, what is missing?
faq.a: Usually one shine everywhere. Make one area matte and one glossy or metal, then check the G ROUGH view for two clearly different greys.
Rarely. A bigger colour jump between neighbours and a shine difference helps far more than turning saturation up.

faq.q: How many colours should a popping car have?
faq.a: Two or three plus one accent. White or black works as the quiet colour that lets the accents sing.

mistakes.symptom: Everything is glossy and still looks flat
mistakes.cause: One shine across the whole car gives the sim nothing to separate
mistakes.fix: Make the neighbour matte or satin; keep gloss for the hero.

mistakes.symptom: Chrome trim looks dark and dull
mistakes.cause: Chrome with Use source paint takes the paint underneath: a dark colour gives dark chrome
mistakes.fix: Lighten the stripe colour first, or choose Satin Chrome or Candy instead.

mistakes.symptom: The hero zone has no effect
mistakes.cause: A zone above it claims the same pixels (the upper zone wins)
mistakes.fix: Drag the hero zone to the top of the left column.

protips: Warm paint on a matte surface next to cool paint on metal reads richer than the same colours on one shine.
Keep the door centre calm: the number must stay readable, so the pop belongs on the hood, roof and lower body.
Compare with the SOURCE view often; if your change barely differs from it at arm's length, push the contrast, not the saturation.

articles.title: Aggressive and mean: dark, sharp, one hot accent
articles.summary: An aggressive car is dark and mostly flat, with sharp-edged graphics (chevrons, razor lines) and one hot accent that looks like a warning. Shine belongs only on the sharp parts.
articles.what: Buyers who type "look mean", "more aggressive" or "badass" want menace: a deep black or gunmetal body with low shine, angular shapes that point forward, and a single hot colour (red, orange, toxic green) used sparingly like a warning light. Menace comes from restraint and sharp geometry, not from piling on effects.
how: Make the body dark and flat. Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.

Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Flat Black (metal 0, roughness 250, coat 255) or Matte (metal 0, roughness 200, coat 160). with BASE COLOR set to Use solid color #0c0d10 (a near-black keeps a little shape).

Add the sharp graphics as their own zone: Under APPLY AREA press Draw box and drag a rectangle over the part on the flat sheet (hood, roof, side, bumper). Open PATTERN and choose Chevron (tidy zigzag Vs) or Razor Wire (wavy barbed-wire strands), set Paint mode to Blend and Scale (pattern) to 0.5 so the lines read fine across the whole car.
Give the graphics zone a gloss edge against the flat body: choose Gloss (metal 0, roughness 30, coat 16) with Use solid color in your hot accent, for example #d8141c.
Keep the accent small: lower lip, mirrors, a thin line along the beltline. Everything else stays dark.

Open the preview strip: R METAL is the metal, G ROUGH the roughness (dark is mirror), B COAT the clearcoat (16 is the glossiest). Check them against the numbers above. The accent should be the only loud thing.

deep.heading: Why dark and flat reads mean
deep.body: Low shine hides soft reflections, so the shape looks like one solid mass. Roughness 200 to 250 with coat 160 to 255 absorbs light; a thin gloss accent (roughness 30, coat 16) then looks wet by comparison.

deep.heading: Angles beat curves
deep.body: Chevrons, razor lines and hard diagonals point the eye forward and read as speed and attitude. Round, soft patterns (swirls, florals) read friendly. Keep the pattern fine (Scale (pattern) 0.4 to 0.6) so it does not turn into a big blob on the car.

deep.heading: One accent rule
deep.body: A single hot colour on about a tenth of the car looks like a warning. Two accents look like a toy.

combos.why: Aggressive is stealth plus one warning colour.
Forward-pointing chevrons add speed to menace.

faq.q: How do I make my car look mean?
faq.a: Dark flat body, sharp chevron or razor graphics, and one hot accent colour in a small area.
Black or gunmetal with red, orange or acid green. White bodies can work if the graphics are black and sharp.

faq.q: Can I do aggressive without black?
faq.a: Yes: any deep colour on a matte finish with black angular graphics and one contrasting accent.

faq.q: Should it be glossy or matte?
faq.a: Mostly matte or satin. Keep gloss for the accent so it flashes.

mistakes.cause: Too many accent colours or soft round patterns
mistakes.fix: One accent, sharp angular pattern, black ground.

mistakes.symptom: The pattern turns into big blotches
mistakes.cause: Scale (pattern) left at 1.0 on a whole-car zone
Dark number on a dark body
mistakes.fix: Keep the number plate area light or outlined; see readable on TV.

protips: A near-black like #0c0d10 keeps a little shape; pure black on a flat finish looks like a hole.
Put the hot accent low (rocker, splitter) so it reads as a base of danger rather than a stripe.

articles.title: Clean and classy: two colours, one stripe, calm finish
articles.summary: Classy is restraint: one dominant colour, one accent, white or black as the quiet colour, a single fine line, and a soft gloss or satin finish with no busy texture.
articles.what: When someone asks for clean, classy, elegant or "less busy", the answer is subtraction. Use a limited palette (about 60 percent one colour, 30 percent an accent, 10 percent trim), keep the shapes simple and aligned across the car, and pick a finish with a soft sheen instead of loud effects.
how: Choose the palette first: one dominant colour, one accent, and white or black as the quiet colour (for example #f2f2f2 white with #c8102e red, or #0d0d10 near-black with #d4a017 gold).

Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.

Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Gloss (metal 0, roughness 30, coat 16) for a showroom look, or Satin (metal 0, roughness 95, coat 70) for a modern one. and set BASE COLOR to Use solid color.

Add one stripe as its own zone: Under APPLY AREA press Draw box and drag a rectangle over the part on the flat sheet (hood, roof, side, bumper). Give it the accent colour with Gloss, or Satin Chrome with Use source paint for a fine metal line.
Line things up: the stripe on the side should continue the colour of the bumper or hood; check the left and right sides match.
Leave numbers and sponsors on clean areas with strong contrast. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing, and judge it in the sim at an angle to the sun.

deep.heading: The 60-30-10 rule
deep.body: About 60 percent one dominant colour, 30 percent an accent and 10 percent trim looks designed. Five colours look cheap. White or black as the quiet colour lets the accent carry the look.

deep.heading: Finish choice sets the mood
deep.body: Gloss (roughness 30, coat 16) is crisp and traditional. Satin (roughness 95, coat 70) is modern and forgiving. Pearl (metal 100, roughness 40, coat 16) adds soft light. Avoid heavy flake or holographic effects when the goal is calm.

deep.heading: Alignment is the polish
deep.body: Lines that continue across panels (side band into bumper, hood stripe over roof and trunk) read as one design. A stripe that breaks at a seam reads amateur.

faq.q: How do I make it look clean?
faq.a: Cut it down to two colours and one stripe, use gloss or satin, and align every line.

faq.q: It looks too busy, what do I remove?
faq.a: Remove the pattern layers first, then any third colour, then extra stripes.
Either. Gloss is traditional, satin is modern. Do not mix both on the same body area.

mistakes.cause: Too many colours or a loud texture on a big area
mistakes.fix: Reduce to two colours plus trim and remove the pattern.

mistakes.cause: Zones drawn separately on the flat sheet
mistakes.fix: Check both sides and each panel on the CAR view; use mirror copies.

mistakes.cause: Everything one finish and one colour
mistakes.fix: Make the stripe a different shine from the body.

protips: A fine line (thin box) reads more expensive than a fat stripe.
Satin black with a chrome hairline is the safest premium combination.

articles.title: Make it look expensive
articles.summary: Expensive is depth and restraint: a deep candy or pearl on the big areas, a fine metal line, a limited palette and no cheap texture. Chrome is for accents, not the whole car.
articles.what: Buyers say "make it look expensive", "premium" or "high end". The tells are a deep wet colour (candy over metal), a soft pearl or satin, a hairline of real metal and a very short colour list. Cheap looks come from flat primaries, five colours and big chrome areas that show every flaw.
how: Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.

Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Candy (metal 200, roughness 15, coat 16). Set BASE COLOR to Use solid color and pick a deep colour: oxblood #5a0a14, midnight #0a1a3a or emerald #0b4a32. Set Color Depth to 65 or 100 for the deepest glaze.
Add depth with a spec overlay: BASE > SPEC OVERLAYS, + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, choose Pearl Micro or Gold Flake, Strength 30 to 50. It changes shine only.
Add one hairline of metal: draw a thin box along the beltline or lower edge, choose Satin Chrome (metal 250, roughness 45, coat 40) and BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only).
Keep numbers crisp white or gold on a clean door area.

Open the preview strip: R METAL is the metal, G ROUGH the roughness (dark is mirror), B COAT the clearcoat (16 is the glossiest). Check them against the numbers above. Candy should read low roughness and coat 16. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing, and judge it in the sim at an angle to the sun.

deep.heading: Depth is the tell
deep.body: Candy is a polished metal response (metal 200, roughness 15, coat 16) under a colour you choose, which is what gives that look-into-it depth. Colour Depth runs 0 (no tint), 15 (glaze), 65 (rich), 100 (deepest).

deep.heading: Chrome goes small
deep.body: Large mirror areas show every panel flaw and flare in the sim. A hairline or trim of chrome reads as jewellery; the whole car reads as a prop.

deep.heading: Fewer colours
deep.body: A limited palette (two or three plus an accent) is the single strongest expensive signal. Gold, silver or white as the one accent.

faq.q: How do I make my car look expensive?
faq.a: Deep candy or pearl on the body, one fine metal line, two or three colours, no busy patterns.
Oxblood, midnight blue, emerald, black with gold, white pearl with silver.
As trim, yes. As the whole car it looks like a show prop and shows every flaw.

faq.q: Candy over black looks black, why?
faq.a: Candy tints what is under it; with a black ground there is nothing to glow. Use a brighter metallic ground or a lighter candy colour.

mistakes.cause: Dark colour on a dark ground
mistakes.fix: Choose a richer, lighter candy colour and raise Color Depth only until it glows.
Keep overlays at 30 to 50 and Scale small.
Use Satin Chrome with a gold source colour so it picks metal.

protips: Hairlines beat stripes: a one-pixel-feeling line along the beltline lifts the whole car.
Check the G ROUGH view: premium surfaces show smooth, even dark areas, not noisy ones.

articles.title: Make it look fast: direction, taper and low colour
articles.summary: Speed reads from forward-pointing lines, tapered stripes, a darker lower body and sharp contrast at the nose. Soft, round, centred patterns slow the car down.
articles.what: Buyers say "make it look fast", "look quick" or "sense of speed". A car looks fast when lines lead the eye forward, shapes taper toward the rear, the lower body is dark so the car looks planted, and the nose carries the strongest contrast. A static car cannot move, but it can point.
how: Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.
Set the body calm: Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Gloss (metal 0, roughness 30, coat 16). with a solid colour.

Add speed lines: Under APPLY AREA press Draw box and drag a rectangle over the part on the flat sheet (hood, roof, side, bumper). Open PATTERN and choose Chevron or Pinstripe, set Paint mode to Blend, Rotate (pattern) so the lines run front to back, and Scale (pattern) to 0.5.
Darken the lower body in its own zone (a Draw box along the rocker) with Matte and a deep colour, so the car looks lower and planted.
Put the strongest contrast at the nose: a bright hood stripe or splitter colour, fading toward the rear.

Open the preview strip: R METAL is the metal, G ROUGH the roughness (dark is mirror), B COAT the clearcoat (16 is the glossiest). Check them against the numbers above. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing, and judge it in the sim at an angle to the sun.
aliases: give it a sense of speed

deep.heading: What the eye reads as speed
deep.body: Lines that run lengthwise, shapes that narrow to the rear, and a visual weight low on the car. Centred circles, flowers and swirls read static.

deep.heading: Keep patterns fine
deep.body: Whole-car patterns at Scale (pattern) 1.0 look like big stickers. Between 0.4 and 0.6 they read as streaks.

deep.heading: Contrast at the nose
deep.body: Strong contrast near the front pulls the eye toward the direction of travel.

faq.q: How do I make the car look fast?
faq.a: Forward-pointing lines or chevrons, a dark lower body and the strongest contrast at the nose.

faq.q: Do stripes make a car look faster?
faq.a: Lengthwise stripes do; vertical or round shapes do not.
Gloss or candy looks quicker than a flat primary; matte gives a stealthier speed.
Not as a real effect, but fine tapered streaks with a speed-line pattern at small scale are the nearest honest look.

mistakes.fix: Rotate the pattern so lines run front to back and check on the CAR view.

protips: A dark rocker makes the whole body look lower, which reads faster.
Use the same direction on both sides: check both sides on the CAR view; the left and right panels can run opposite ways on the flat sheet.

articles.title: Stand out in a pack: be seen from far away
articles.summary: To be found in a field of 40 cars, use a colour nobody else has, a bold two-colour split and one bright accent, and avoid mid-tones that blend into the track and sky.
articles.what: Cars at distance are a few pixels wide. Colour and value decide recognition, not detail. Pick a hue that is rare on track (hot pink, cyan, lime, orange on white), use big blocks instead of fine texture, and make the roof and hood readable from the chase camera.
how: Choose a colour pair that is rare on track and strongly different in value: black with hot pink, white with orange, dark blue with lime.

Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.
Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Gloss (metal 0, roughness 30, coat 16). for the dominant colour with Use solid color.
Make the roof and hood a big block of the second colour: Under APPLY AREA press Draw box and drag a rectangle over the part on the flat sheet (hood, roof, side, bumper).
Put the contrast on the nose and roof, because the chase camera and overhead views see those most.
Check small: zoom out until the car is a few pixels. If you can still tell it from the others, it works. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing, and judge it in the sim at an angle to the sun.

deep.heading: Distance is value, not detail
deep.body: At pack distance fine detail averages to grey mud. What survives is large blocks with a strong light-versus-dark split and a hue that does not match its neighbours.

deep.heading: Rare hues beat bright hues
deep.body: Red and blue are the commonest on track. Hot pink, cyan, lime and orange on white are rare, so they get noticed first.

deep.heading: Roof and hood
deep.body: The chase camera and overhead views show the roof and hood most; give them the loudest block.

faq.a: A rare hue, a two-colour split with strong light and dark, big blocks.

faq.q: Does chrome help me stand out?
faq.a: Chrome flashes in sun but turns dark in shade; a bright colour is more reliable.

faq.q: What if my sponsor colours clash?

articles.title: Readable on TV: numbers and sponsors that survive distance
articles.summary: Put strong light-on-dark or dark-on-light contrast behind every number and logo, keep the door centre calm, and avoid sparkle, chameleon or busy pattern directly behind them.
articles.what: iRacing is seen at speed and at distance. Numbers and sponsors need a clear value split from whatever sits behind them. This is the discipline that makes a design usable: the number plate area is quiet, and the loud finishes live on other panels.
how: Decide the number area first: the door centre is where the number lives (roughly 0.30 to 0.65 of the side height, front 22 percent being the fender).

Make a calm base behind it: Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.

Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Gloss (metal 0, roughness 30, coat 16) or Satin (metal 0, roughness 95, coat 70). with a flat solid colour.
Put loud effects (flake, chrome, candy, patterns) on the hood, roof, lower body and bumpers, never on the number area. Use RESTRICT TO LAYERS so the numbers and sponsors layers stay untouched.
Check contrast: white on dark or black on light. If your number is mid-grey on mid-grey, change the plate colour, not the number.
Zoom out in the preview until the car is tiny and read the number. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing, and judge it in the sim at an angle to the sun.

deep.heading: Value contrast, not hue
deep.body: The camera is not colour-picky; it needs lighter-versus-darker. Red on blue can vibrate and still be unreadable because both are mid-value.

deep.heading: Why effects hurt
deep.body: Sparkle, chameleon and pattern change brightness every few pixels, which breaks the edges of letters. A flat finish keeps the edges sharp.

deep.heading: Layers protect your art
deep.body: On a layered template, a body zone limited to Car Paint leaves the numbers and sponsors layers exactly as they are.

The door centre, around 0.30 to 0.65 of the side height.
Yes, give logos a clean background; a calm base carries them.

articles.title: Stealth and murdered-out: black on black
articles.summary: Murdered-out is flat black on every surface with only a whisper of shine difference. Use Flat Black or Matte for the body, a satin trim and a near-black pattern so detail shows only in the sun.
articles.what: A stealth look wants no colour at all: matte black body, black wheels, black trim. The art is in the subtle shine differences (flat against satin against a gloss hairline) so the shape still reads in the sim.
how: Press + Add Zone. Under COLOR choose Remaining for the whole car, or press PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the colour you want to restyle. On a layered template also tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers and sponsors stay untouched.

Under BASE press Base Material, open the FOUNDATIONS category, then the Foundation Bases shelf, and choose Flat Black (metal 0, roughness 250, coat 255) for the deadest body, or Matte (metal 0, roughness 200, coat 160). and set BASE COLOR to Use solid color #0a0a0c.
Add a hidden layer of detail: a second zone over the lower body or hood with Satin (metal 0, roughness 95, coat 70) in #0d0d10. In the sim the satin catches light while the flat stays dead.
Optional pattern: open PATTERN, choose Carbon Fiber or Hex Carbon, Paint mode Blend, low Opacity (about 15 to 25), Scale (pattern) 0.5. It shows only in sunlight.
Keep numbers and sponsors readable: leave them on their own layer or use a pale grey number (#e8e8ea).

Open the preview strip: R METAL is the metal, G ROUGH the roughness (dark is mirror), B COAT the clearcoat (16 is the glossiest). Check them against the numbers above. Matte reads bright in G ROUGH and B COAT should not be at 16. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing, and judge it in the sim at an angle to the sun.

deep.heading: Flat is a spec, not a colour
deep.body: Flat Black is metal 0, roughness 250, coat 255, the deadest foundation; Matte is roughness 200, coat 160; Satin is roughness 95, coat 70. A dark body made of all three levels reads as black from far and shows form up close.

deep.heading: Colour stays near black
deep.body: Pure #000000 on a flat finish looks like a hole. A very dark grey (#0a0a0c to #1a1c20) keeps edges and creases visible.

deep.heading: Quiet textures
deep.body: A low-opacity carbon or hex pattern adds depth without breaking the stealth. Use Blend mode so the pattern keeps the dark base.

articles.title: Make it look wet: razor gloss and deep colour
articles.summary: A wet look is the tightest highlight a plain paint can have: Wet Look (metal 0, roughness 15, coat 16), a deep dark colour, and dull neighbours so the shine reads by contrast.
articles.what: Buyers say "make it look wet", "freshly waxed", "glossy" or "show shine". Wet comes from the lowest roughness a non-metal paint allows, the deepest coat, a dark or saturated colour that gives the reflections something to sit on, and a matte or satin area nearby that makes the gloss obvious.
how: Press + Add Zone, set COLOR to Remaining (or PICK COLOR FROM CAR on the colour to restyle), and tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS.
Under BASE press Base Material, open FOUNDATIONS > Foundation Bases and choose Wet Look (metal 0, roughness 15, coat 16). with BASE COLOR on Use solid color.
Pick a deep colour: black #0b0b0e, oxblood #5a0a14 or midnight #0a1a3a. Dark grounds show reflections best.
Optional: open BASE > SPEC OVERLAYS, + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, choose CC Wet Zone, Strength 30 to 40, for slightly uneven glossy clear patches.

Put a Matte or Satin zone beside it (for example the roof or a lower band) so the wet area reads by contrast. Check the preview strip: R METAL, G ROUGH (dark is mirror), B COAT (16 is glossiest). Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing.

deep.heading: The numbers
deep.body: Wet Look is metal 0, roughness 15, coat 16: the tightest highlight a dielectric paint can have. Gloss is roughness 30, so Wet Look is twice as tight. Coat 16 is the deepest clearcoat; larger values are duller.

deep.heading: Contrast makes wet
deep.body: Gloss only reads against something duller. A car that is all gloss looks plain; the same gloss beside a matte roof looks wet.

articles.title: Satin and modern OEM: soft sheen, no hard reflections
articles.summary: Modern factory and wrap looks live on Satin (metal 0, roughness 95, coat 70) or Semi-Gloss (roughness 55, coat 40): a soft broad highlight in a grey, white or deep colour.
articles.what: Satin reads as a premium factory or vinyl-wrap finish. It hides small surface flaws, never looks cheap, and works under sponsors. The step down from gloss is Semi-Gloss, then Satin, then Eggshell, then Matte.
how: Press + Add Zone, set COLOR to Remaining (or PICK COLOR FROM CAR on the colour to restyle), and tick Car Paint under RESTRICT TO LAYERS.
Under BASE press Base Material, open FOUNDATIONS > Foundation Bases and choose Satin (metal 0, roughness 95, coat 70). with BASE COLOR on Use solid color.
Pick a modern colour: slate grey #6b6f76, cement #a0a3a8, deep green #123524, or a pearl white #e9e9e6.
For a metallic satin choose Satin Pearl (metal 100, roughness 90, coat 60) instead; for a flat metal choose Matte Metallic (metal 225, roughness 140, coat 100).

Add a single gloss detail (trim or lower splitter) in Gloss so the satin reads. Check the preview strip: R METAL, G ROUGH (dark is mirror), B COAT (16 is glossiest). Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing.

deep.heading: The ladder
deep.body: Gloss roughness 30, Semi-Gloss 55, Satin 95, Eggshell 140, Matte 200, Primer 215, Flat Black 250. Each step rubs the highlight out wider and flatter.

deep.heading: Why it is forgiving
deep.body: Broad soft highlights hide panel flaws and do not blow out under sun, so satin suits both clean and busy liveries.

articles.what: A full-chrome car is the loudest look there is and shows every flaw. Used as trim, numbers or accents it reads as jewellery. When a buyer wants a show car, pick the chrome tier that matches the mood: mirror, dark or satin.

articles.title: Worn and patina: faded paint, rust and honest wear
articles.summary: Weathering is roughness up, coat value up (the clearcoat wears off), colour faded, with wear at edges and the lower body. Lower Base Strength so your own colours show through.
articles.what: Barn-find, race-worn or sun-faded looks come from finishes that fade and pit the paint, plus a restrained amount of rust. Put wear where real wear happens (front, lower panels, roof) and keep it fine.
how: Make a zone on the area to weather (Draw box on the lower half or roof) or Remaining on Car Paint.
Under BASE press Base Material and search Sun Faded (bleached), Surface Rust, Die-Back Patina, Chalked Paint or Hardware: Battle Worn.
Lower Base Strength to 50 to 70 so your own paint shows through (0 is your paint, 100 is the full finish).
Add detail: BASE > SPEC OVERLAYS > Salt Spray Corrosion or Galvanic Corrosion at Strength 30 to 40.
Check at 100 percent zoom: wear should read as fine detail, not blotches. Press RENDER, then Ctrl+R in iRacing.

deep.heading: The spec of wear
deep.body: Worn finishes push roughness up and the coat value up (B 16 is glossiest, so wear is a bigger number): Sun Faded is about metal 2, roughness 168, coat 137; Surface Rust about metal 83, roughness 131, coat 104 (catalogue averages).

deep.heading: Where wear sits
deep.body: Edges, lower panels, front and roof. Matte and low-metal finishes look more weathered than chrome.
